title: Ship a Production-Shaped Pipeline and Break It On Purpose
objective: Run one batch path and one stream path into a documented shared warehouse, with contracts, a DAG, tests, one bounded backfill, and instrumentation — then recover from an injected failure and show the test command still passes.
whyThisMatters: Separate tasks can hide glue. A production-shaped system is the glue: two inbound paths, one contracted warehouse, a scheduler that tells the truth, and a recovery you can repeat. This is the point of the path, not a slide deck of tools.
evidence: Documented commands that run the batch job, the stream consumer, the validator, the DAG, and the test suite
A query showing warehouse rows from both the batch source and the stream source, with the join or shared key documented
Before and after counts plus an incident or recovery note for the injected failure
A captured passing test-command run after recovery
Git history spanning the work, not a single final commit
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The repository contains a batch job, a stream consumer, a contract file, a DAG, and a test command, each runnable from a documented command.
Batch and stream paths write to a documented shared warehouse table or to two tables joined by a documented key, and a query shows rows originating from both sources.
An injected failure and its recovery are captured with before and after counts and an incident or recovery note.
The documented test command is run after recovery and passes.
Git history contains more than one commit for this task's work.
